Definition: Does the government maintain a digital business register?
Comments: No credible evidence found after searching business registration digital, online company registration; processes manual via Ministry of Commerce, Commercial Registry.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A 2026 company-search guide confirms Equatorial Guinea 'has no functional public online commercial registry'; the Registro Mercantil (Ministry of Justice) requires in-person or agent-based filing, with certified extracts taking 5-15+ days. The 'Ventanilla Única Empresarial' one-stop shop (since 2019) scans intake documents into an internal inventory but is a filing tool, not a searchable digital register, and processed only 63 dossiers in its first months of operation. World Bank B-READY 2025 rates Equatorial Guinea's business-entry 'Public Services' pillar in the bottom 20% of economies globally. On balance the evidence still supports Value Code 1 (No functioning digital business register), but given the VUE's partial internal digitisation this is a borderline case — flagged for human review rather than upgraded on this evidence alone.

revision_notes: World Bank Equatorial Guinea Digital Economy Diagnostic (2024) — a primary, authoritative source — confirms the country lacks a unified digital population register or interoperable digital identity ecosystem, and recommends 'streamlining the digital civil registry and implementing a digital identity ecosystem' as a priority reform, alongside a 'currently absent national interoperability framework'. A pilot Computer System of the Civil Registry (SIREC), launched 2018 by the Ministry of Justice, covers only vital-event registration, not a continuously updated population register. Confirms Value Code 1 (No), now backed by a dated, primary World Bank source in place of the original uncited claim.
